**Consequences.** M6's gate has its run: the harness reports Rivals transferring among themselves (1,093
Transfers in 200 games, 63 of them the Generator's), and M6-S3's second box and M6-S4's second box have
their harness evidence in the epic. The four Dispositions stay distinct as M6-S1's and M6-S4's first boxes
ask. For the owner:

- **M6's Rivals are now the player's competition for the Board.** Three of the four take the Board's
  harder half, so the Quests left to the policy are easier: its mean difficulty fell from 53.8 (M5) to
  46.2, its failures from 23.1% to 14.9%, its Wealth after 20 years from 232,781 to 189,977, and two of its
  200 games ended in Bankruptcy, where M5's run had none. The policy is M5's and declines every Transfer
  Offer (161 in the run); a smarter policy, and whether it should ever accept, is a decision after these
  counters (the M6 risk table).
- **The Rivals are no threat in the Rankings**: the player's Guild is first by Fame at 89.5% of year-starts
  and by Wealth at 91.6%, and from year 5 its mean place is 1.1 or better.
- **A Rival's folds come from Levels outrunning its income.** A Rival whose Heroes seldom die sees their
  Levels rise to 8 to 10 at a Roster of 4, and its wages with them, while its place along the Quests it can
  staff pays what it paid; the training yard speeds the climb. The pass moves where each Disposition sits
  on that curve, not the curve. Changing it is a rule for the owner (a Rival choosing harder Quests as its
  Heroes grow, letting its dearest Hero go, or choosing which facilities it builds, a new weight), or values
  the player pays too (`wagePerLevel`, `xpPerTrainingDay`, `hallMaintenancePerGrade`).
- **`transferAppetite` does two jobs**: the chance a Rival seeks a Transfer, and, with its Roster, whether
  it consents. At a third or more a Rival sells itself below `rivalRosterMin` and item 5's chain returns, so
  every row sits below a third and `miserly` (0.1) never deals at the Rosters it keeps. A consent floor at
  `rivalRosterMin` in `transferAnswer`, the Generator's own guard (DL-59 item 5), would free the appetite
  to range to 1; it is a rule change the pass did not need and left to the owner.
- **Transfers are few and mostly between two**: 5.5 a game, 831 of 1,093 between `ambitious` and
  `reckless`, a tenth back to a Guild that had sold the Hero, none within the 90-Day lock.
- **`steady` and `miserly` still sit at the floor holding Wealth** at 47% and 37% of their year-starts
  (the target's line is half): their rows' hiring bars (60 Upkeeps) are seldom reached, and a lower bar
  made `steady` fold more. Their Rosters never decay below the floor (DL-60's need), which was the
  verification's concern.
- **The measures are where M4's and M5's were**: a Turn alone 1.5 ms, a year of fast forward 1.6 s, a save
  after 20 years 98.5 MiB (data-model §7: 5 ms, 1 s, 20 MiB), recorded, not chased (DL-08).
- **The engine's test content keeps M6-S1 to S4's Disposition rows** (item 8); a later pass that wants the
  engine's tests to prove the core's own rows would mirror them there and re-measure those tests' margins.

## DL-70 — M4 verification corrections: the Board names the Skills its Encounters' Checks read; tests that kill six mutants

**Status:** Accepted · **Date:** 2026-09-26 · **Decided by:** an agent (the M4 verification's fixer),
on findings it confirmed; no rule, default or content value changes

**Context.** M4 was verified after its merge into v1.0-dev (`c1161b5`) by gate, acceptance, mutation,
design, decision-log and CLI passes. The mutation pass ran 79 mutants of M4's rules; 73 were killed
and 6 survived. The CLI pass found two problems. `show board` names Skills that help in no Check.
The help for `preview` leaves out its Synergies section. DL-61 to DL-64 are reserved for other lines
of work, so this entry is DL-70.

**Decision.**

1. **`show board`'s "Skills that help" lists the Skills of the Quest's Encounters.** Each is listed
   once, in the order the Quest meets them, and a key content lacks is left out (data-model rule 5).
   A Quest drawn before M4 has its Encounters drawn on the way (DL-42 item 7), so it still shows its
   template's Skills.
   - *Why.* From DL-42 on, the Check reads each Encounter's `skillKeys` and never the Quest's own,
     which are copied from its template. The column therefore named Skills that help in no Check.
     On Guard the caravan (travel and combat) it named Trapcraft, and on The sickness at the mill
     (social and arcane) Herbalism and Field surgery. It also left out the Skills that do help.
   - *What it supersedes.* The sentence of DL-42's Consequences that has `show board` read the
     template's `skillKeys`.
   - *What stays.* `partyFor` still reads the template's `skillKeys`. The Board's "Demands" column
     still shows the template's demands: a summary of the kind of work, while each Check weighs its
     own Encounter's demands.
   - *Versions.* `configVersion` stays 6 and `contentVersion` stays 8.
2. **`help` names `preview`'s Synergies section** (DL-45 item 7) beside its other sections.
3. **Tests that were too weak.** Each surviving mutant is now killed by a new or stronger test; no
   assertion was loosened.
   - *The band over the whole sequence* (DL-42 item 11). A band read over only the Encounters a
     Party reached passed every test. A new test sends a Party that comes through its first
     Encounter and dies of it: one success of three is a failure.
   - *The Guildmaster Regard writers* (DL-43 item 4). All four amounts were pinned at ±1, so a Hero
     written with a Patron's amount passed. The one-test-each tests now pin the four apart.
   - *A plain success* (DL-43 item 4, DL-46 item 2: a success is any band but `fail`). Three mutants
     passed because every test resolved a strong success or a failure:
     - the Patron's Regard written as on a failure;
     - the Heroes' success bonus kept for a strong success only;
     - the Guildmaster's Regard written for a Hero killed on the Quest.

     A new `questsConclude` test resolves two Encounters of three, with a Death. It pins every
     amount apart and checks each Regard, and that the dead Hero gets none.
   - *`heroRegardDecays`.* Its Hero-only condition is unreachable through `decayHeroRegard`, which
     visits only Heroes the world holds. The exported predicate is now tested directly.

**Consequences.** No rule or value changes, so DL-55's run and report stand. The first build's other
front end (M7) should take the Skills that help from the Encounters too.

## DL-71 — M6 close verification corrections: errata to DL-63 and DL-69; tests that kill 32 mutants of the M6 harness

**Status:** Accepted · **Date:** 2026-09-27 · **Decided by:** an agent (the M6 close verification's
fixer), on findings it confirmed; no rule, default or content value changes

**Context.** M6's close (DL-63, DL-69; `c27b34f` to `95e03a7`) was verified by merge, counters,
balance and mutation passes. The mutation pass found 32 mutants of the harness's M6 code
(`harness/src/play.ts`, `harness/src/sweep.ts`) that every test let through. The other passes found
four statements in DL-63 and DL-69 that the evidence they cite contradicts, and three test comments
the balance pass left stale. DL-63 and DL-69 are accepted, so they are corrected here, as DL-53
corrected DL-40 and DL-41.

**Decision.**

1. **Errata.** The decisions of DL-63 and DL-69 stand, and so do their values, the run and its report.
   - *DL-63 item 2* says the main line's two saves, loaded under the merged CLI, "gain
     `transferredOnTurn` on every Hero and `offers`". They gain `transferredOnTurn` only. A save the
     main line made at schema 2 already carries `world.offers`, an empty map: the main line's
     `document.ts` creates every World with it, and its validator requires it. The 2 → 3 step
     (`transferredOnTurnField`, `engine/src/serialise.ts`) touches only `world.heroes`. Rechecked on
     five saves made by `47d6df6`'s CLI and harness: each one, migrated, differs from its original only
     by `transferredOnTurn: null` on every Hero (81 of 81 in the largest).
   - *DL-69 item 7 and its Consequences* say `miserly` "never deals at the Rosters it keeps". It deals
     seldom, not never. Every way a Rival deals asks for its consent (`transferAnswer`, DL-57 item 3):
     the Heroes it keeps through the deal times its `transferAppetite` must reach one. At 0.1 that
     means a Roster of 10 or more to buy and 11 or more to sell. `miserly` keeps such a Roster seldom
     (above 8 at 4.0% of its year-starts). In the run it bought 4 Heroes and sold 18 (12 to
     `ambitious`, 6 to `reckless`), as item 9's own table gives. Read: `miserly` "deals seldom, and
     only at a Roster of 10 or more".
   - *DL-69 item 7's characters* say `ambitious` "hires and deals most". It deals most, not hires most.
     `reckless` hires the most: 1.62 recruits a Guild-year against `ambitious`'s 1.02, and still the
     most with the Transfers bought added (about 1.73 against 1.16). `ambitious` deals the most (980
     Transfers bought or sold, against `reckless`'s 944) and buys the most Heroes by Transfer (558
     against 435). Read: `ambitious` "builds first, deals most and buys the most Heroes by Transfer".
   - *DL-69 item 9's last point* says "5.5 Transfers a game in every five-year block". 5.5 is the rate
     over the whole twenty years. The four five-year blocks hold 228, 426, 209 and 230 Rival-to-Rival
     Transfers, which is 1.14, 2.13, 1.05 and 1.15 a game. Read: "5.5 Transfers a game, and some in
     every five-year block". The target of item 4 ("2 to 30 a game and some in every five-year block")
     is met as it said.
2. **Tests that were too weak.** Each surviving mutant is now killed by a new test, shown red with
   the mutant applied and green without it. No assertion was loosened.
   - *The M6-S3 assertion, out of the player's Guild and on a later Turn* (P01, P06). The one test
     forced a Transfer into the player's Guild on Turn 0. So a check that caught only Transfers in,
     and a check that resumed one entry past the last it read, both passed. But out of the player's
     Guild is the way the assertion guards (the Transfer Generator never takes from it). A new
     `play.test.ts` test has the player's Guild send a Hero to a Rival on Turn 2, after two advances
     already checked, with Rivals that deal whenever they can trading among themselves before it. It
     expects the assertion to stop the game there, naming that entry and "out of". The mutant that
     swaps "into" and "out of" in the assertion's prose dies with them.
   - *`readAdvance` across two afternoons* (P10, P11). Reading every `hero.transferred` from the
     History's start, or marking none read, passed. The one test kept the same debtor in debt, and the
     set de-duplicated the position. A new test has a sound seller sell on one afternoon and fall into
     debt before the next. It expects the first sale not to be judged again.
   - *`recordGame` passing the in-debt Transfers to the counters* (P12). An empty set in its place
     passed. A new test plays a game in which every Guild is below `bankruptcyFloor` from the first
     night and none goes bankrupt in it, with the dealing Rivals, and ends with 44 such Transfers. It
     expects `afternoon-seller-in-debt` to count exactly the play loop's Rival-to-Rival positions, and
     `afternoon` to count the rest of the afternoon's Transfers.
   - *`sweepTotals`' M6 sums* (S01, S02b, S03b, S04b, S05b, S09, S10b), *the report's M6 cells*
     (S15b, S16 to S28, S31 to S34) *and the generation range's bounds* (S11, S12). The sweep test's
     fixture holds no Transfer, offer or fold, and no Roster or Wealth on a bound, so only labels and
     zeros were asserted. A new `sweep.test.ts` test gives its two games made-up M6 counters, Wealth
     and Guild-years. It asserts the totals (sold back, by side, offers, each Disposition, grades by
     Disposition) and every M6 cell the report writes from them:
     - the Wealth rows with Transfer fees, and the share of Wealth spent on Transfers;
     - the Transfers by direction and by way, and the sold-back sentence;
     - by side and the seller-by-buyer matrix;
     - the offers' mean fee and Standing;
     - the purchases a Guild-year;
     - each Disposition's character row;
     - the grades by Disposition.

     Another gives two year-starts on the range's bounds (Rosters 4 and 8, Wealth 300 and 700) and
     expects none counted below or above.
3. **Stale comments.** `dispositions.test.ts` and `rivals-build-and-buy.test.ts` said the test
   content's Disposition rows are the core's, but they are M6-S1 to S4's (DL-69 item 8). The CLI's
   `transfer.test.ts` gave `ambitious` weighing a Transfer "three times in four", but it is three in
   ten since DL-69's `transferAppetite` 0.3. The comments are corrected; the tests are unchanged.

**Consequences.** No rule, default or content value changes: `configVersion` stays 10, content
version 14 and schema version 3. So DL-69's run and `harness/reports/m6-2026-09-27.md` stand, and
the run is not repeated. DL-63 and DL-69 are read with item 1's corrections.

## DL-72 — Merging the main line (M0 to M6 complete) into M7: both sides kept whole, no version changes

**Status:** Accepted · **Date:** 2026-09-27 · **Decided by:** an agent (merging v1.0-dev into
`m7-integration`), recording a merge; it chooses no default, content value or version

**Context.** M7-S1 (`045f3e6`, DL-64) was built on `m5-integration`'s tip `83df01e`. Since then

build against that engine, so the main line is merged in first.

   order: the merged log differs from v1.0-dev's only by DL-64's 105 lines. DL-65 to DL-68 stay

   `tsconfig`, CI workflow, `.npmrc` or `.node-version`, since `83df01e`. So the workspaces and
   pins are DL-64 item 1's: `npm install` changed nothing in the lockfile, and `npm ci` succeeds

3. **`content/src/imports.test.ts` merged without conflict, both additions kept**: the main line's

   its test, and M7-S1's tests that `web/`'s `.test.ts(x)` files may import `@heroesim/content/node`
   and a component may not. Checked for a semantic clash: M7-S1 made `boundary.test.ts` also write

## DL-73 — The web's views, part 2: the rest of the CLI in the browser, one engine selector for the rules notice, the game as a file, and the page's own words (M7-S3 part 2)

**Status:** Accepted · **Date:** 2026-09-27 · **Decided by:** an agent (M7-S3 part 2's implementer)

**Context.** Part 1 (DL-66) built the shell, the header, the Board with dispatch, the Roster with
Hero pages, time and the narrated log, and nine rows of the epic's table of CLI commands. Part 2
builds the rest: the Market (buy, sell), the Hall (build), the Rankings by Fame and by Wealth, the
Unattached pool and recruiting, Transfers in and out, Transfer Offers accepted and declined, equip
and unequip, and the "new rules available" notice with its `rebase` button (D1). With them comes every
other CLI command still unticked: `show guilds`, `show roster|hall|guildmaster <guildId>`, `show
patrons`, `show history`, `save --as`, `load` and `help`. The boxes: every CLI command has a browser
equivalent (box 2); the event and Potential boxes (1 and 3) must still hold; box 4 (360px) is
M7-S4's. The same rules bind as in part 1: nothing in `web/` computes a rule (ADR-0007, principle 12),
and only `state/` and `content.ts` import the engine's values (DL-65 item 7).

**Decision.**

1. **One engine selector: `newRules(meta, config)`** (`engine/src/actions/rebase.ts`, exported). It
   returns the game's `configVersion` and the later one of `config` while the game's is behind, and
   otherwise `null`. The page passes `defaultConfig`, so the notice shows exactly while a `rebase`
   would adopt newer rules. The action itself refuses only equal versions: a save from a later
   release can still be rebased down, but no front end offers that. Three tests in
   `rebase.test.ts`. No config field, event, content value or version changes.
2. **No other engine change.** Every other number the new views show is a document field or an
   existing selector's answer, the ones the CLI's views read:
   - the Market: `marketStock`, `sellPrice`, `holdings`;
   - the pool: `unattachedHeroes`, `signingFee` at the player's Guildmaster's Negotiation, and
     `signingRefusal`;
   - Transfers: `transferFee` at the paying Guild's Guildmaster's Negotiation, the rule
     `transferIn` and `transferOut` charge by; and `offersTo`;
   - the Guilds and the Hall: `upkeep`, `rankings`, `nextImprovement`;
   - the Guildmaster and the Patrons: `ageOf`, `baseStat`, `regardBand` over `regardValue`,
     `patronRegardFor` and `guildmasterRegardForGuild`;
   - the History: `entriesFor`.
3. **The views' rows live in `state/`**, beside part 1's `selectors.ts`:
   - `world-views.ts`: the Guilds, the Rankings, another Guild's page, a Hall, a Guildmaster, the
     Patrons and the History;
   - `trade-views.ts`: the Market, the pool and the offers;
   - `game-file.ts`: the save's text, its file name and the rules notice;
   - `names.ts`: the name helpers they share. `selectors.ts` now uses them too, and exports
     `linesOf` and `modifierWords`.

   The words are the CLI's (`cli/src/render.ts`, `commands/market.ts`, `commands/transfer.ts`),
   less the ids a command line takes. One change of word: a Guild's controller reads "Yours" for
   the player's Guild where the CLI says "Player", as the page speaks to the player as "you"
   throughout. `state/game.test-support.ts` holds the setups the page's tests need but may not
   build themselves, since tests outside `state/` import only the engine's types: an offer made by
   the engine's own `offerTransfer`, rules behind this release's, Items held, Wealth. Nothing imports
   it but tests, so it is never bundled.
4. **The page's order.** One column, in the order a Turn reads:
   - the header, the rules notice when there is one, and Time;
   - the Board, the Roster, the Transfer Offers and the Unattached pool;
   - the Market, the Hall, the Guildmaster and the Patrons;
   - the Rankings and the Guilds;
   - "Since your last action", the History and "This game".

   The epic's sections keep its order; part 2's sit beside the ones they concern. The page is now
   long, so an index of links under the header takes the keyboard to each section's heading. A
   refusal is sticky at the top of the viewport, so a refusal of a play made far down the page is
   seen where it was made.
5. **What each play looks like.**
   - *Buy and sell* take a quantity, a whole number from 1. The input's `min` and `max` are the
     numbers the Market shows, so a browser's own form check stops a purchase of more than is
     there. Anything else the engine refuses, in its words.
   - *Build* is one button per facility, naming the next Improvement; only the player's own Hall
     has them.
   - *Recruit* is a button on each pool card and on the Hero's page, which opens from the pool.
   - *Equip, unequip and Transfer out* are on the player's Hero's page. Equip is offered for each
     piece of gear the Guild holds; the engine picks the slot. Unequip is offered for each slot
     that holds an Item. Transfer out picks the Guild from every other Guild in play, each shown
     with the fee it would pay.
   - *Take in* is on another Guild's Roster, which opens from the Guilds, and on its Heroes' pages.
   - *Accept and decline* are on each Transfer Offer.
   - *No preview.* Unlike dispatch, none of these plays is enabled only when it would succeed. The
     CLI previews none of them, and the engine's refusal says why in a sentence. Whether a Guild
     would consent is shown only by trying, as in the CLI.
6. **The game as a file: `save --as` and `load`.** The CLI's `save --as <file>` writes the save as
   canonical JSON, and `load <file>` makes a file the save.
   - *Export.* "This game" offers "Export this game": a download of the game's `serialise`d text,
     named `heroesim-<seed>-day-<n>.json`. It is the file the CLI writes. The download uses an
     object URL and requests nothing, and the bundle gate still passes.
   - *Load.* "Load a save file" reads the file chosen and hands its text to the reducer's `load`
     play, which reads it under the engine's own config (DL-20, DL-65). It is offered before a
     game and with one in hand. A save's unknown content keys are listed as the CLI's warnings.
   - *A new game in place of one.* "Start a new game" shows the new-game form again, saying the
     game in hand goes unless exported, with a way back. This is the CLI's `--force`, and it is
     the "new game" button part 1 left for later.
   - *What stays M7-S4's.* Saves kept in IndexedDB and their measure; the Node test that the CLI
     loads an exported file; the Playwright journeys. `game-file.ts` is in `state/`, so M7-S4's
     `saves.ts` can take `saveText` from it or join it there, answering DL-65's note on where
     `serialise` may be imported.
7. **The rules notice** (D1). While `newRules` is not `null`, the page shows a "New rules available"
   section naming both `configVersion`s, with "Adopt the new rules" as a `rebase` play. The log then
   narrates `world.rules-adopted`, and the notice goes.
8. **The History.** The whole History or a Guild's, newest first, 20 entries a page, part 1's
   `historyPageSize`; buttons go to the newest, newer, older and oldest pages. The CLI prints the
   whole History oldest first. The page shows both newest first, as a Hero's page does, because
   what the player wants first is what happened last. A folded Guild's History can still be chosen.
   A Hero's History is on their page. The CLI's `show history <id>` for any other entity, a Patron
   say, has no control of its own; the whole History holds those entries.
9. **`help`: the page's own words.** Each section is a region with a heading and a sentence, its
   accessible description, saying what the section is for and what its controls do. The sentences
   are adapted from the CLI's usage text, without the numbers config sets (the fee factor). Each
   control is named by what it does ("Recruit Una Barrowby", "Build Sickroom", "Take … in").
   `app.test.tsx` holds every section to it, before a game and with one, and holds every button and
   field to a name.
10. **Stop buttons re-pointed** (DL-66 item 4). `transfer-offer` now reads "Answer the offer" and
    goes to the Transfer Offers; `pool-refreshed` reads "See who joined the pool" and goes to the
    pool.
11. **Corrections to M7's earlier work**, found while building on it:
    - *Where a Hero on no Roster is* (part 1). A Hero on no Roster was "at the Hall" on their page.
      Now they are "in the Unattached pool", or "on no Roster" once they have left it.
    - *The ending's refusal* (DL-65's map). It named "Turn 540", while the page names only Days and
      its header says "The game ended on Day 180". It now names the Day. The CLI's own words keep
      the Turn.
    - *Busy text.* "Playing the Turns…" showed for any play; it now shows only while an advance or
      a fast forward runs.
    - *A comment.* `narrate.ts` pointed to a `stopActions` in `selectors.ts` that does not exist;
      it now points to `nextFor` in `views/time.tsx`.
12. **Box 3 still holds, over the whole page.**
    - *What changed in the test.* The Guildmaster section now names the concept, in the CLI's words
      for Judgement: "how sharp the Potential hints read". So `views/hero-page.test.tsx` searches
      each Hero's page for the word, and the whole page, every section, for the sentinel numbers.
    - *A new test.* It opens, from the page, every pool Hero's page and every Hero's page on every
      Rival's Roster.
    - *Tried.* Two deliberate leaks were each caught and then reverted. A pool row showing a
      Potential number failed both page tests. A Rival's Roster row showing one failed the new test.
13. **Box 4 checked, not proved.** A scratch Playwright spec, not committed, measured `scrollWidth ≤
    innerWidth` at 360×800 and 1280×800. It covered a 67-character Guild name, every section after a
    fast forward, and a Hero's page, a pool Hero's page, a Rival's Guild page and one of its Heroes'
    pages, each open. It also covered the Rankings by Wealth, a refusal while scrolled, and the
    new-game form over a game. It passed, and the phone screenshots were read. The box stays
    M7-S4's.
14. **The table** in the epic has every row ticked, and box 2 is ticked. The `new`, `show hero` and
    `save --as`/`load` rows now say what is built.

**Consequences.** Every CLI command has a browser equivalent, driven through the page's controls in
`views/actions.test.tsx`, `views/world.test.tsx` and `app.test.tsx`. M7-S4 adds saves in IndexedDB
beside "This game", the Node test of an exported file, the journeys and the 360px box. `offerTransfer`
has no control: the CLI has no command for it, and only a player's Guild answers offers, so today it
is always refused. `npm run lint` and `npm run typecheck` pass. `npm test` passes 104 files and 2,188
tests, none skipped; 53 of them are new. `npm run build -w web` exits 0 through the gate: 470.61 kB
(136.49 kB gzipped), "no network or filesystem reference". `npm run e2e -w web` passes 4.

## DL-74 — M7 verification corrections: anyone the History names found by name, a load that closes the last game's pages, a journey that recruits, a bundle gate that reads every comment and URL, a build that refuses a Node built-in; tests that kill 29 surviving mutants

**Status:** Accepted · **Date:** 2026-09-27 · **Decided by:** an agent (the M7 verification's fixer),
on findings the verification confirmed; no engine rule, config default, content value or version
changes

**Context.** M7 (M7-S1 to S5 and the merge: DL-64 to DL-68, DL-72, DL-73; `045f3e6` to `c6f2199`)
was verified by acceptance, boundaries, play, mutation and decisions passes, and each finding below
survived a skeptic. In short:

- one test timed out in most full runs;
- the browser could not open a dead, retired or departed Hero, whom the CLI reaches by id;
- no Playwright spec recruited, though the Gate says Playwright proves it;
- the bundle gate could be blinded by two innocent strings, and let `ws://`, `wss://` and
  protocol-relative URLs through;
- three places said the gate refuses a Node built-in, which never reaches the bundle;
- the import check missed a template-literal `import()`;
- an open page survived loading another game;
- the log's filter unticked itself after every play;
- 29 mutants survived every test.

DL-64, DL-65, DL-66, DL-67, DL-68 and DL-73 are accepted, so what changes or corrects them is
recorded here, as DL-71 did for DL-63 and DL-69.

**Decision.**

1. **A test bounded, not sped up** (`views/hero-page.test.tsx`). "Potential is never rendered … on
   the page of every Hero in the pool and on every Rival's Roster" opens every such page. It takes
   2 to 3.5 s alone and 3.5 to 4.5 s in the web project. In a full `npm test` it timed out against
   Vitest's 5 s default in 12 of the verification's 13 runs (5.1 to 6.3 s). The describe now
   has `{ timeout: 30_000 }`, the repository's way with a slow test (`engine/src/boundary.test.ts`,
   `rng.test.ts`): the timeout bounds a hang, not the speed.
   - *Erratum to DL-68.* Its "`npm test` passes 107 files and 2,235 tests" held on the run it
     reports, but not reliably on this machine.
2. **Anyone the History names, found by name** (the CLI's `show hero <heroId>` and `show history
   <entityId>`). In the twenty-year sample, 113 of 185 Heroes the world holds are dead and 36 are on a
   Roster, and the History names 5,871 Heroes. The page opened a Hero only from a Roster or the pool.
   - *The control.* The History gains "Find someone in the History by name". It lists every Guild,
     Hero, Guildmaster and Patron the History has an entry for whose name holds what is typed, case
     aside. Each is listed with what they are ("Hero, dead", "Hero, retired", "Hero, no longer in the
     world", "Hero of The Lantern", "Guildmaster of …", "Patron", "Guild, folded"), 20 at most, in
     name order, with how many matched.
   - *What opens.* "Read <name>" makes them whose History is shown. A Hero the world still holds,
     dead and retired ones included, opens on their page (`HeroPage`): Attributes, Stats with hints,
     Milestones first, then their History. That is the CLI's `show hero` for any Hero. Anyone else,
     a Hero gone from the world among them, has their entries listed newest first, as a Guild's are.
   - *Where it lives.* `state/world-views.ts`: `findInHistory`, and `historyView` now takes any
     entity. A name is the world's row's while it holds one, else the label of the entity's newest
     entry. Nothing computes a rule.
   - *What is not named.* Quests and Parties are not listed. A Quest is called by its template's
     name, which many Quests share (27,721 Quests in the sample); their entries are read in the
     whole History, as DL-73 item 8 decided.
   - *Supersedes* DL-73 item 8's "The CLI's `show history <id>` for any other entity, a Patron say,
     has no control of its own" for Heroes, Guildmasters and Patrons.
   - *Erratum to DL-73.* Its Consequences, "Every CLI command has a browser equivalent", overstated
     `show hero` and `show history` until now. The epic's three rows that take an id say what is
     built, and its table's lead-in names `app.test.tsx` beside `views/*.test.tsx`.
3. **The journey recruits** (the Gate: "created, advanced, dispatched, recruited, saved to
   IndexedDB and reloaded; Playwright proves it"; DL-67 item 7 gains the step).
   `e2e/journey.spec.ts`, at both sizes, now recruits after the dispatch. It picks the pool Hero
   with the lowest signing fee among those who would sign at a fee the Guild can pay. It checks
   four things: the log's sentence, Wealth less the fee, the Hero on the Roster and gone from the
   pool. After the reload and the load, the Roster reads as it did when saved.
   `e2e/layout.spec.ts` adds the History's search, the Guildmaster's long name found, and a Hero's
   page opened from it, at 360px and 1280px.
4. **The bundle gate reads the text as built** (`scripts/check-bundle.mjs`; supersedes DL-64
   item 5's "comments stripped first" and its `http(s)://` pattern).
   - *Comments.* v1's stripper, `/\/\*[\s\S]*?\*\//`, also matched inside strings. So everything
     between a string holding `/*` and a later one holding `*/` went unchecked: an accept of
     `'image/*'`, then `'*/*'`. Stripping is dropped. The shipped bundle holds one comment,
     `/*$vite$:1*/`, and no other `//`. A comment that names an address now fails the gate: a false
     alarm is put right by hand, where a hidden call would never be seen.
   - *URLs.* Any scheme followed by `//`, or `//` alone, protocol-relative, is a URL literal, checked
     against the allow-list. That covers `ws://` and `wss://`, and `//host` in a CSS `url()`, an
     `@import` or a `src`: on `https://heroesims.pages.dev` it resolves to `https://host`. Every `//`
     in the shipped bundle is one of the five allow-listed identifiers, so the gate passes it
     unchanged: 2 files, "no network or filesystem reference".
   - *Tried.* The verification's probes, as `bundle.test.ts` fixtures: `fetch(` between `'text/*'`
     and `'*/*'`, and a URL between `'image/*'` and `'*/*'`; `wss://`, `ws://`, plain `http://`, a
     protocol-relative `src`; a URL in a `.css` `url()`, a protocol-relative `@import`; a
     `<link href="https://…">` and a `fetch(` in `index.html`; a licence comment's URL. Each fails
     the gate.
5. **The build refuses a Node built-in** (`vite.config.ts`, the plugin `heroesim:no-node-builtins`).
   - *Why.* Vite replaces a Node built-in the page imports with an empty stub, with only a warning.
     The specifier never reaches the bundle, and the gate passed it. Turning the warning into an error
     with `onLog` was tried: Rolldown logged it and still built, exit 0.
   - *What.* The plugin resolves before Vite's own. It stops the build on `node:*` or any name in
     Node's `builtinModules`, subpaths such as `fs/promises` included, from the page or a dependency.
     The real build passes.
   - *The test.* `bundle.test.ts` builds a one-script page with the page's own configuration for each
     of `node:fs`, `fs` and `fs/promises`: each build fails, naming the specifier. The same page
     without the import builds.
   - *Words corrected.* ESLint's message for `web/src` and `web/tsconfig.json`'s comment said the
     bundle gate refuses a Node built-in. They now name the build. DL-64 item 8 made no such claim.
6. **The import check reads a template literal** (`web/src/imports.test.ts`; DL-65 item 7). An
   `import(\`@heroesim/engine\`)` was recorded as "(computed)" and passed, although the bundler
   resolves it as it resolves a quoted one. `ts.isStringLiteralLike` now reads both, with a snippet
   that proves it.
7. **A game started or loaded shows nothing the last one had open.** The Roster, the pool, the
   Guilds, the Board and the History kept the open Hero, Guild, Quest or History in component state.
   After a load they showed a page the player never opened, or "That Hero is no longer in the world.".
   - *The fix.* The state gains `games`, how many games have been put in hand; a new game or a load
     adds one, and any other play or a refusal does not. It is a fourth field beyond the epic's four,
     beside DL-65 item 3's three. `App` keys the sections from the Board to the History by it, so they
     start afresh with each game. The header, time and "This game" are not keyed.
8. **The log's filter holds from play to play** (DL-66 item 6). "Only what concerns <Guild>" was
   reset by the key that restarts the log's paging after each play. The filter now lives in `Log`, and
   only the paging is keyed. So the choice holds while the game is in hand, as the History's does,
   and a new game or a load starts it afresh (item 7).
9. **Tests that were too weak** (the mutation pass). Each surviving mutant is now killed. Each was
   shown red with the mutant applied and green without it, by a script in the fixer's scratch space
   that is not committed. No assertion was loosened.
   - *The Transfer fee among a Rival Hero's Attributes* (W2). `selectors.test.ts` pins it, for every
     Rival Hero, to the fee at the player's Guildmaster's Negotiation, which is the actions' fee. It
     also checks that the seller's Guildmaster gives another number for some of them.
   - *A loaded save's warnings* (R20, R21, R22; DL-65 item 3, DL-73 item 6). A save with a Hero's
     Background this content lacks (`sea-born`, the CLI's rule-5 test) stores one warning. It holds
     through an advance and a refusal. It is gone after a new game or a clean load. The page lists it
     under "This game" (`reducer.test.ts`, `views/world.test.tsx`).
   - *The log's sentences* (N3, N5, N6, N10, N11, N12, N15, K9, K11, K14, K16). `narrate.test.ts` pins
     every sample's sentence word for word. It adds 17 variants: a success and a strong success; a
     consumable's heal of one Day, its bonus and its re-roll; the player's own sale; a Transfer with no
     offer; each end of an offer; each way a Guild folds and the game ends; a Hero made on a Roster; a
     healing with no Trait; gear back from a retired Hero and as a Guild folds; Morale that rose.
   - *The stop for a live Transfer Offer* (N13). An offer made by the engine's `offerTransfer` is
     narrated as "Stopped: a Transfer Offer: <Rival> offers <fee> Wealth for <Hero> until the night of
     Day <n>.", the CLI's words less its ids.
   - *The refusals* (J6, J7, J9, K3, K4, K5, K6, K7, K8). `rejections.test.ts` pins every kind's
     sentence in its world. It checks every kind for ids with a world and without one. It pins four
     sentences with no world: "That Hero", "that Guild", "That Quest", "your Guild".
   - *IndexedDB's own adapter* (P3; DL-67 item 1). `saves.test.ts` drives `browserSaves` over a
     stand-in IndexedDB whose read-write transactions commit or abort when the test says. A save
     and a delete are reported only after the commit. A write abandoned at commit with a
     `QuotaExceededError` is `failed`, in the browser's words, and keeps nothing. The store is keyed
     by the save's name, which also kills P2 without Playwright.
   - *The gate's `http://`, `.html` and `.css`* (B5, B9, B10): item 4's fixtures.
   - *The fixes themselves.* Undoing each fails its tests: the comment stripper and the
     `http(s)`-only pattern restored, the plugin removed, `isStringLiteral` restored, the sections
     unkeyed, `games` never counted, the log keyed whole, Heroes left out of the search, the History
     never opening a Hero's page.

**Consequences.** Every CLI command's browser equivalent reaches what the CLI's reaches by id, save a
Quest's and a Party's own History, which stays in the whole History. The Gate's journey is proved in
Playwright, recruit included; the deploy (M7-S5's first box) is still the orchestrator's. The bundle
gate refuses what it says it refuses, and the build refuses what the gate cannot see. No engine,
content or CLI file changes: `configVersion` stays 10, content version 14 and schema version 3.
`npm run lint` and `npm run typecheck` pass. `npm test` passes 107 files and 2,475 tests, none
skipped, 240 of them new, in each of three full runs in a row. `npm run build -w web` exits 0
through the gate: 481.59 kB (140.03 kB gzipped), "no network or filesystem reference". `npm run e2e
-w web` passes 16.

## DL-75 — M7 close: the Pages project created on classic Pages, the first deploy, and a check of the deployed page

**Status:** Accepted · **Date:** 2026-09-27 · **Decided by:** an agent (the orchestrator closing
M7), carrying out the owner's INPUTS 7.8 and 7.9 answers; it chooses no default, content value or
version

**Context.** M7's stories and their verification (DL-64 to DL-68, DL-72 to DL-74) left M7-S5's
first box to the orchestrator: deploy with DL-68's command and prove that the URL serves the build
and a fresh browser creates a game and saves. INPUTS 7.8 names a Cloudflare Pages project
`heroesims`, production branch `v1.0-release`, at `https://heroesims.pages.dev`; 7.9 a local
`npx wrangler login` and no secret anywhere. This machine was already logged in (v1's deploy,
DL-30 on `feature/poc`); the project did not exist.

**Decision.**

1. **The project is created on classic Cloudflare Pages, with `--force`.** Wrangler 4.141.0, asked
   to create a Pages project that does not exist, delegates to "the latest version of Cloudflare
   Pages, now part of Cloudflare Workers": it runs its framework detection, refuses at a
   workspace's root, and would make a Workers project served from a `workers.dev` address, not the
   `pages.dev` Pages project 7.8 names. Wrangler's own notice offers `--force` to create the
   project directly on Pages. So, once, from `web/`:
   `npx wrangler pages project create heroesims --production-branch v1.0-release --force`.
   Wrangler says only creation needs it: the project now exists, so DL-68's
   `npm run deploy` runs against Pages unchanged and never passes `--force`.
2. **The first deploy** ran `npm run deploy` from `v1.0-dev` at `ba38eb5` (M7 merged; the code the
   `m7-web` tag carries, which adds only documents): two files uploaded, the bundle 481.59 kB
   (140.03 kB gzip) with the gate passing, the deployment published to the production branch and
   `https://heroesims.pages.dev` answering 200. The release deploy follows README's procedure from a
   checkout of `v1.0-release` at the tag.
3. **The check is committed, not only run:** `web/e2e/deployed.live.ts` with its own
   `web/playwright.live.config.ts`, run by `npm run e2e:live -w web`, in the shape of M7-S4's
   measure (DL-67): kept out of `npm run e2e`, which never needs the network, and out of CI (7.10).
   At 360×800 and 1280×800 it creates a game, plays a Day, saves in IndexedDB, reloads, loads the
   save at the same Turn, finds no horizontal overflow, and fails if the page requests anything
   from another origin. Both passed on 2026-09-27. README's Deploy section names it as the step
   after each deploy.
4. **Nothing of the account enters the repository.** No token, account id or `.wrangler/` state is
   written here; `web/src/deploy.test.ts` (DL-68) still guards it.

**Consequences.** M7-S5's first box is met and M7 closes, tagged `m7-web`, with one box open:
M7-S4's twenty-year round trip through IndexedDB takes 3.6 s against 1 s (DL-67), and the lever is
the save's size, a data-model decision for the owner. Left to the owner: Cloudflare is folding
Pages into Workers; a later wrangler may stop offering classic Pages, and moving the page to a
Workers project would change its address and DL-68's command.

## DL-76 — The module contract: the `Module` interface in the engine's own types, slices and streams made by `ensureModules`, the three hooks as entries of the phase list, a slice migrated without a version from the core, and byte identity with `m7-web` on 200 × 20 (M8-S1)

**Status:** Accepted · **Date:** 2026-09-27 · **Decided by:** an agent (M8-S1's implementer), where
the epic's sketch had to meet the engine's real types or left a choice open; no default, content
value, `configVersion` or schema version changes

**Context.** M8-S1 writes the module contract (ADR-0005 as amended 2026-09-25, data-model §3.4,
approach §2, N6). The epic sketches the interface with names that predate the engine (`Event`,
`Failure`, `StreamName`, `createWorld(content, config, seed, setup, modules = [])`), and says a
slice is migrated with `migrateSlice(slice, fromVersion)` while data-model §3.4 says the core
never reads inside a slice and a module keeps its own version there. Its first box asks that with
no module installed every harness counter equals the M7 tag's run, byte-equal saves included.

**Decision.**

1. **The interface, in `engine/src/modules.ts`, in the engine's own types.** `Module<Slice>` has
   `id`, `streamName?`, `createSlice(ctx)`, `validateSlice(slice)`, `migrateSlice?(slice)` and
   `onMorning?`/`onAfternoon?`/`onNight?(world, slice, ctx)` returning
   `ModuleResult = { events: EngineEvent[]; stop?: StopReason }`. Where it differs from the epic:
   - `Event` is `EngineEvent` and `StopReason` is stops.ts's (M8-S2 adds `module` to it);
   - `Failure` is `SliceFailure = { at, detail }`, a place in the slice and prose, which the
     validator reports as a `module-slice` refusal at `$.world.modules.<id>` followed by `at`, so a
     refusal names the module;
   - `streamName` is a `string`: `StreamName` is the union of the core's streams;
   - **`migrateSlice(slice)` takes no `fromVersion`.** Only the slice holds its version (§3.4),
     and the core, which never reads inside a slice, cannot pass it; the module reads its own.
     It is called on every present slice of an installed module that has the method, after the
     core's migration chain and before the validator, and returns the slice as it is when current;
   - `createWorld(seed, setup, deps)` and `deserialise(text, deps)` keep their signatures and take
     the modules as `deps.modules`, none when absent, as every entry point takes them (approach §3,
     pre-M0 review D1); the placeholder `Module` of `config.ts` is replaced by this one;
   - hooks receive the world typed `Readonly<World>`, a shallow promise that M8-S2's frozen-world
     test makes binding.
   A module that throws in a hook or in `createSlice` throws `ModuleError`, naming `moduleId` and
   `during` (the hook, or `createSlice`), with what it threw as `cause`: modules are code, so it is a
   programming error.
2. **Registration.** `installedModules(deps)` refuses, with a RangeError, an empty id, two modules
   with one id, and a stream named as a core stream or another module's. `ensureModules(world,
   seed, deps)` gives the world each installed module's stream it lacks, seeded as a core stream is
   (`createStreams(seed, [name])`) and kept in `world.rng` beside the core's, then each slice it
   lacks from `createSlice`, in registration order. `createWorld` calls it last, after the Market
   refresh; `advance` calls it on its copy beside `ensureStreams`, so a save made before a module was
   installed gains its stream and slice the first time it is played (DL-25's rule for streams).
   `world.modules` and `world.rng` already hold both, so the document's shape is unchanged and the
   schema stays at version 3, with no migration.
3. **The hooks are three entries of the flat phase list**, named `onMorning`, `onAfternoon` and
   `onNight`, at approach §2's positions: after the Market refresh, after Quests in flight advance,
   and after the pool refresh, before Transfer Offers expire and the ending checks. pipeline.test.ts's
   literal holds them there. `PhaseContext` gains `modules`. Each entry calls the installed modules
   that have the hook, in registration order, with the Turn's world, the module's slice (changed in
   place, in the Turn's copy) and a minimal context: `config`, `content`, `turn`, `emit`, and `rng`,
   the module's own stream bound, every draw of which throws for a module that registered none.
   M8-S2 adds the selectors and the `effects` API. A hook's events join the Turn's at its position
   and the History; its `stop` is accepted by the type and not yet acted on (M8-S2). `advance` plays
   on a copy and appends only after the whole Turn, so a throwing module leaves the document it was
   given as it was.
4. **Loading and validation.** `deserialise` runs the chain, then `migrateSlices`, then the
   validator. `validate` has each installed module validate its present slice (`module-slice`) and
   warns, with `unknown-module`, of a slice no installed module owns, which is kept and never read,
   as rule 5 keeps an unknown content key; an installed module whose slice is absent is not asked. A
   module that throws migrating or validating a save's slice refuses the load rather than throwing,
   since a save is outside the engine's control. Data-model §3.4 and §6 say so.
5. **The core never reads inside a slice.** modules.test.ts reads every non-test source file of
   the engine, comments removed as controller-reads.test.ts removes them, for `world.modules`,
   `world?.modules` and `world['modules']`, and finds them in `modules.ts` only.
6. **A harness fingerprint.** `DocumentMeasures.fingerprint` is SHA-256 of a game's last save, and
   `sweepFingerprint` is SHA-256 over one line per game, in seed order, of its seed, a tab and that
   fingerprint. The play report gives it in one row ("Fingerprint of every seed's last save") and
   `npm run harness` prints it, so a later M8 story, or the M8 close, shows in one line whether
   anything moved a game. It changes no counter.
7. **Byte identity with `m7-web`, proved on 200 seeds × 20 years.** A detached scratch worktree of
   the tag (`d792a76`, the same tree as `a83f9d9`), `npm ci`, and one scratch driver run unchanged
   against both trees: 16 child processes, each playing its seeds with the harness's own `playGame`
   under the core content and `defaultConfig`, as `npm run harness` does (not validated per Turn),
   and writing per seed the SHA-256 of `serialise` of the last document and the SHA-256 of the
   game's harness record: `countGame` with the Rivals' afternoons, the observations, the Turns
   played, the policy's refusals and the harness assertion. At `m7-web` the deps carried no
   `modules`; on this branch, `modules: []`. **All 200 seeds agree, saves and counters alike.**
   The two 200-line tables are byte for byte equal (each table's SHA-256
   `9d1d5ec0a2d52457c681e868dd9ded00088cb691731bae6f77b7a58042d28477`), over 4,314,028 Turns
   played (198 games ran the full 20 years, 2 ended), 51,885,237 History entries and
   20,630,181,665 characters of saves; `seed-0001`'s last save is 113,281,366 characters, the
   length the M6 report's replay records. The tag played in 67.1 minutes, this branch in 61.8, and
   the engine, content and harness played here are the trees this commit carries. In
   `sweepFingerprint`'s form, the fingerprint of `m7-web` over `seed-0001` to `seed-0200` × 20
   years is `7c71caae3e08c4405e14f3fae3a0c8cc95d1f6deac55e9b80de45a929c07458b`: a later 200-seed
   `npm run harness` with no module installed prints that value unless something moved a game.

**Consequences.** With no module installed the engine plays as `m7-web` did; the three hook
entries cost an empty loop a Turn. M8-S2 makes the context real (selectors, `effects`), acts on a
hook's `stop` with a `module` stop reason, and freezes the world a hook sees. Left open for M8-S2
and M8-S3: a module's own event types (`probe.fired`) are not in `EngineEvent`, so either the union
gains them or `ModuleResult.events` widens to entries of any type, which M8-S4's narration fallback
then meets.

## DL-77 — Hooks, effects and stops: a read-only world, typed effects through the core's own rules, a module's events typed by its module beside the engine's union, and a `module` stop reason (M8-S2)

**Status:** Accepted · **Date:** 2026-09-27 · **Decided by:** an agent (M8-S2's implementer), where
the epic names the context, the effects and the stop but leaves their shape open, and where DL-76
left the typing of a module's own events to this story; no default, content value, `configVersion`
or schema version changes

**Context.** M8-S2 makes the three hook positions real (ADR-0005 as amended 2026-09-25, data-model
§3.4, approach §2, N6). The epic asks that a hook's `ctx` carry `emit`, `rng` (the module's own
stream only), `config`, `content`, `turn` and read-only selectors; that a module change a core
table only through a typed `effects` API (`adjustMorale`, `adjustWealth`, `adjustRegard`, `injure`,
`offerQuest`) so the core stays the only writer of its rows; that a module's `stop` halt fast
forward with its reason and the CLI and the web show it; that a module assigning
`world.heroes[id].morale` fail a frozen-world test; and that hook order among several modules be
registration order. DL-76 left open how a module's own event types (`probe.fired`) sit beside
`EngineEvent`, which must not need editing for each module.

**Decision.**

1. **The World State a hook sees is read-only, in the types and at run time.** A hook is given the
   Turn's world as `ReadonlyWorld = ReadonlyDeep<World>` (read-only.ts): every property `readonly`,
   every list a `ReadonlyArray`, so `world.heroes[id].morale = 0` does not compile; and at run time a
   Proxy view of the Turn's copy, which reads through to the world as it stands (an effect applied a
   moment ago included) and throws a TypeError on any set, define, delete, prototype or
   extensibility change of any object reached from it, arrays' in-place methods included. The hook's
   throw becomes a `ModuleError` naming the module (DL-76), and `advance`, which plays on a copy,
   leaves the document it was given as it was. A Proxy rather than a frozen copy: nothing is copied,
   and reads stay live. `ctx.config` and `ctx.content` are views of the same kind, since a module
   writing to them would change the rules or the content for the whole game. The slice is the one
   thing a hook changes directly, through its `slice` argument; through the world it too is
   read-only. With no module installed no view is made.
2. **The context.** `ModuleContext` is `config`, `content` (read-only), `turn`, `rng` (the module's
   stream, DL-76), `emit` (the module's own events, item 4), `select` and `effects`. `select` binds
   the core's selectors to the Turn's world: `unattachedHeroes`, `offeredQuests`, `rankings`,
   `upkeep`, `effectiveStats`, `moraleBand`, `regard` (`regardValue` of a holder's map) and `age`
   (`ageOf`); rows they return are read-only views. **It has no `playerGuild`:** a module is a rule,
   and no rule asks which Guild is the player's beyond `plan.md` §1's three accepted exceptions
   (ADR-0002; controller-reads.test.ts would refuse it). A real module that needs the player's Guild
   asks the owner first.
3. **The effects are typed records, each run by the core's own rule and explained by the core's own
   event** (effects.ts). `ModuleEffect` is the union of `AdjustMorale { heroId, delta }`,
   `AdjustWealth { guildId, delta }`, `AdjustRegard { holderId, entityId, delta }`, `Injure { heroId,
   typeKey, days }` and `OfferQuest { patronId, templateKey? }`, told apart by a `kind` named as the
   epic names the functions; `ctx.effects` has one function a kind, derived from the union, so a
   kind a real module adds (the epic's risk table) adds its function. Each returns `{ ok: true,
   effect, events }` or, for a change its rule does not allow, `{ ok: false, rejection: { effect,
   reason } }` having changed nothing, as an action does; a programming error (an id the world lacks
   or of the wrong table, a delta that is not a whole number, or for Regard a finite one, an Injury
   type content lacks, Days below 1, a Patron with no such template) throws, and so fails the Turn
   naming the module. Each event names the module as `moduleId`, and where its type has a cause the
   cause is `module`:
   - `adjustMorale`: `changeMorale` (morale.ts), held inside `moraleMin`–`moraleMax`,
     `hero.morale-changed` always, as every discrete change; refused `hero-gone` for a Hero dead,
     retired or gone from the pool.
   - `adjustWealth`: the Guild's Wealth, which may go below 0 as Upkeep may take it, and a new
     event, **`guild.wealth-changed`** `{ guildId, moduleId, before, after }` (not a Milestone), the
     one change of Wealth no other event records; refused `guild-folded`.
   - `adjustRegard`: regard.ts's `adjustRegard` for the holders the core has: a Patron for a Guild,
     a Guildmaster for a Patron, a Hero or a Guildmaster (Regard for a Guild is read from its
     Guildmaster's), a Hero for another Hero; `patron.regard-changed`, `guildmaster.regard-changed`
     or `hero.regard-changed` only on a band crossing (data-model rule 10, DL-43), through the
     writers the core uses (`patronRegardChanged`, `guildmasterRegard`, `heroRegardChanged`, the last
     two now exported). The entry's `since` is the Turn and its `reason` the module's id; data-model
     §3.2 now says a reason may be one. Refused `holder-gone` for a Hero out of play or the
     Guildmaster of a folded Guild.
   - `injure`: the Days given, a whole number from 1, shortened by the infirmary of the Hero's Guild
     exactly as a Quest's Injury is (`healDays`, `healFactor`; grade 0 for a Hero on no Roster), then
     `inflictInjury`: both now in injuries.ts, which the Quest Engine and `questsConclude` use too, so
     the rule is stated once. `hero.injured` with **`questId: null`** (the type is now `QuestId |
     null`). Refused `hero-injured` (one Injury a Hero), `hero-away` (in a Party, whose return
     applies its own) and `hero-gone`. The Hero State Engine heals it as any Injury.
   - `offerQuest`: the Quest Generator, drawing the template, difficulty and duration and the
     Encounter sequence from the module's own stream (`generateQuest` gains `sequenceStream`, whose
     default, `encounters`, leaves every core draw as it was), so no core stream moves; the Quest goes
     on the end of the Board and may take it past `boardSize`, which only says how far the morning's
     refresh fills it; `quest.offered`. A module with no stream throws.
   `MoraleCause`, `PatronRegardCause`, `GuildmasterRegardCause` and `HeroRegardCause` gain `module`,
   and those events and `quest.offered` and `hero.injured` an optional `moduleId`, absent from every
   event the core makes for itself, so a game with no module writes the same bytes.
4. **A module's own events are typed by the module, beside the engine's union, which never lists
   them** (events.ts). `ModuleEvent<Type, Payload>` is an `Entry` whose `type` is branded in the
   types alone (`ModuleEventType`), and `TurnEvent = EngineEvent | ModuleEvent` is what a Turn
   produces: `advance`, `fastForward` and `runTurn` return `TurnEvent[]` (a phase's rule still
   returns `EngineEvent[]`). The brand is what keeps the union usable: comparing `event.type` with
   an engine type narrows a `TurnEvent` to that engine event exactly as it narrows an `EngineEvent`,
   and a module's event never passes for one; a reader tells a module's event with `isModuleEvent`
   (or `isEngineEvent`, true for a type `milestoneTypes` lists). A module declares its own,
   `ModuleEvent<'probe.fired', {…}>`, and its `ctx.emit` returns that type. The emitter
   (`moduleEventEmitter`) labels participants and adds a Hero's Guild as the engine's does, sets
   `milestone` from the draft (false unless it says so, since the engine's table knows no module's
   types), and refuses a type outside the module's namespace, `<module id>.<what-happened>`, or one
   of the engine's: a module changes a core table only through its effects, so a core event always
   means the core did it. In the History a module's event is an `Entry` like any other, indexed by
   its type, so `byType['probe.fired']` counts it. Every engine-side test's event collectors were
   retyped `TurnEvent[]`; M8-S1's test of a hook's events emitted `world.created`, which the emitter
   now refuses, and emits `announcing.said` instead.
5. **A hook returns every event it made, in the order the History is to hold them.** Its own, from
   `ctx.emit`, and its effects', which it may put before, between or after its own. The core refuses
   (a `ModuleError`) a hook that returns an event not made by that call or one twice, or that leaves
   out an event one of its effects made, since a core row would then change with nothing to explain
   it (principle 11). The events join the Turn's at the hook's position.
6. **The stop.** `StopReason` gains `{ kind: 'module'; moduleId }` (`ModuleStopReason`), always on
   (approach §2: "a module asks for a decision"), reported after `transfer-offer` and before
   `pool-refreshed`. A hook returns it as `stop`; one naming another module or another kind fails the
   Turn naming the module. The hook positions collect the stops in `PhaseContext.moduleStops`;
   `advance`'s `stoppedBecause` is `ended`, else the first module to ask, in registration order,
   else `null`, since a module's stop holds for whoever is watching (DL-33's reading of `advance`);
   fast forward reads it through `PlayedTurn.stoppedBecause` in `stopsOfTurn`. The CLI says
   "Stopped: the probe module asked to stop." after `advance --until` and, since a stop is for
   whoever is watching, `advance --turns n` now stops early on a module's stop and says so, as it
   stopped on an ending; `--until` does not name `module`, which is always on. The web says the same
   sentence with a "Read what happened" button to the log, and a multi-Turn advance there already
   stopped on any stop. Both front ends word `guild.wealth-changed`, a `module` Regard cause
   ("through a module") and, since their narration now takes a `TurnEvent`, give a module's own event
   a line that names its type ("A module's event: probe.fired."), the least that keeps a narration
   map total; M8-S4 owns what that line says and shows the probe's in both logs.
7. **Hook order is registration order** (DL-76's loop), now held by a test with two spy modules
   registered each way round.
8. **No module installed still changes nothing.** The hook positions return at once with no module;
   the injury and generator refactors state the same formulas and defaults; every new payload field
   is optional and absent from the core's events. Checked beyond the suite: `seed-0001` to
   `seed-0016` × 20 years with the harness's own parallel sweep (`sweepPlayInParallel`, core content,
   `defaultConfig`, `modules: []`), run on this change and, from the same tree with the change
   stashed, on M8-S1's commit (`fb7d416`, itself byte-identical to `m7-web` on 200 × 20, DL-76): the
   16 per-seed SHA-256s of the last save agree, and so does `sweepFingerprint`,
   `738516cfea14564e6c22e7753aac3f2ba7dce8ef5ffb30b3df6ee9e437858068`. The 200 × 20 proof is the
   M8 close's (DL-81).

**Consequences.** The contract is now whole: M8-S3's probe applies each effect through `ctx.effects`,
emits `probe.fired` with the applied effects (each result carries its `effect` record, which is
JSON-safe), asks for its stop, and is typed without touching `EngineEvent`. Two things for M8-S3 and
M8-S4 to meet: the harness's `hero.injured` counters find the Guild among an entry's participants
and throw when there is none, so an `injure` of an Unattached Hero would stop a harness run (the
probe injures a Hero on a Roster, or the counter learns to skip); and a front end reading the History
casts each entry to `TurnEvent`, whose module events `isModuleEvent` tells apart. A real
module that needs more reach adds an effect kind to the union with a DL, never a write to a core row.

## DL-78 — The probe module: its tunables on its slice, a stop counted from its last, one draw a night that also picks its targets, a fabricated version 0; the harness installs modules by id and reports a module run against none (M8-S3)

**Status:** Accepted · **Date:** 2026-09-27 · **Decided by:** an agent (M8-S3's implementer), where
the epic names the probe's hooks, slice and harness run but leaves their details open; no default,
content value, `configVersion` or schema version changes

**Context.** M8-S3 writes `engine/src/modules/probe.ts`, a test-only module that proves the module
contract (DL-76, DL-77) end to end: id and stream `probe`; a slice `{ version: 1, hooks:
Record<phase, count>, lastStopTurn }` with `probeStopEveryDays` on it, "because a module owns its own
tunables"; `onMorning` counts, `onAfternoon` counts and asks for a stop every `probeStopEveryDays`,
`onNight` draws one number and "on a threshold" applies one effect of each kind and emits
`probe.fired` with the effect list; `validateSlice` refuses a negative count; `migrateSlice` brings a
fabricated version 0 forward by adding `lastStopTurn`. Its fourth box asks that
`HEROESIM_MODULES=probe npm run harness` run 50 seeds with the probe and report `probe.fired` and the
delta on each core counter it touched. DL-77 left one thing for this story: the harness's
`hero.injured` counters throw on an entry that names no Guild.

**Decision.**

1. **The probe is exported from the engine's index, test-only** (`probe`, `createProbe`,
   `probeDefaults`, `probeId`, `probeSliceFailures`, `probeSliceVersion` and its types), for the
   engine's tests, the harness and M8-S4's test switches. `createProbe(tunables)` makes a probe whose
   slices carry the tunables given; `probe` is `createProbe()`. Both `probe` and `probeDefaults` are
   marked `/* @__PURE__ */`, so a bundle that never installs the probe leaves it out: the web build
   holds none of it (checked on the built bundle).
2. **Every tunable of the probe is a field of its slice, not only `probeStopEveryDays`.** The epic
   names one; the others are its threshold and its effects' sizes, and a literal balance number in
   rules code is a defect (principle 8), so they sit beside it with the same prefix:
   `probeStopEveryDays` 30, `probeFireBelow` 0.02 (a night in fifty, about seven a year of 360
   nights), `probeMoraleDelta` −5, `probeWealthDelta` 25, `probeRegardDelta` 2, `probeInjuryDays` 2.
   A game keeps the values its slice was made with, as it keeps its `meta.config`. The counts are
   keyed by time of day (`{ morning, afternoon, night }`), the epic's "phase". Data-model §3.4 now
   says a module's tunables live in its slice.
3. **The hooks.** `onMorning` counts. `onAfternoon` counts and asks for its stop on the afternoon of
   the Day `probeStopEveryDays` after the Day of its last stop (Day 0 before the first), recording
   the Turn in `lastStopTurn`: reading its last stop makes `lastStopTurn` the state the stop depends
   on, so the version-0 migration that adds it is a real one. `onNight` counts and draws one number;
   below `probeFireBelow` it fires, and the same number, scaled by the threshold (a draw below it is
   uniform below it), picks the Hero among those on the Rosters of the Guilds in play who stand ready
   (in no Party, not injured), in id order, and the Patron, in id order. It applies, in the effects
   API's order, Morale to the Hero, Wealth to their Guild, that Patron's Regard for the Guild, an
   Injury of content's first type by key, and a Quest of the Patron's on the Board (drawn from the
   `probe` stream, DL-77), and emits `probe.fired { roll, effects }`, each effect listed as `{ effect,
   applied: true }` or `{ effect, applied: false, rejection }`, naming the Hero and the Patron (and
   the Hero's Guild, which `emit` adds); it returns `probe.fired` first, then the applied effects'
   events. With no Hero ready it fires on none, the draw taken all the same. Choosing a Hero on a
   Roster meets DL-77's note: every `hero.injured` the probe makes names a Guild, so the harness's
   counters need no change for it.
4. **Its slice read from a save.** `validateSlice` (`probeSliceFailures`) refuses, each failure
   saying "The probe module refuses its slice: …" at its place in the slice (so the validator's
   `module-slice` refusal is at `$.world.modules.probe.…`): a slice that is not an object or not
   version 1; a count that is not a whole number from 0, or of anything but the three times of day;
   a `lastStopTurn` that is neither `null` nor a Turn; a tunable outside its range. Version 0, which
   the probe never wrote, is version 1 without `lastStopTurn`; `migrateSlice` gives it `lastStopTurn:
   null`, as if it had never stopped, and returns anything else as it is for `validateSlice` to
   accept or refuse.
5. **The harness installs modules by id** (`harness/src/modules.ts`). `HEROESIM_MODULES` is parsed
   by `moduleIds`, which refuses an unknown id, an empty one or one named twice; `harnessModules`
   holds the modules the harness may install, only `probe`. A module is code, so a parallel sweep's
   job carries the modules' ids (`ShardJob.modules`, absent with none, so a no-module run writes the
   same jobs as before) and each child installs the harness's own of each id; `idsOf` refuses, before
   any child starts, a module that is not the harness's own, such as a probe with other tunables.
6. **A module run is a run of its own** (`modules.harness.test.ts`). When `HEROESIM_MODULES` names
   modules, `npm run harness` plays `HEROESIM_SEEDS` seeds (50 by default) for 20 years under the
   automatic policy twice, with the modules and with none, one sweep after the other, with the usual
   assertions on both (no refused action, no validator refusal, no broken assertion, every save round
   trips, the replay identical), and writes `harness/reports/m8-<ids>-<date>.md` (`reportPath` now
   takes `m<n>-<name>`); the creation and play runs skip. The counters gain M8's (`GameCounters`,
   `SweepTotals`): `moduleEvents`, each module event type the History indexes, by count; and
   `moduleEffects`, the core's events naming a module as `moduleId`, by module and type, read from
   the entries of `effectEventTypes`, the seven types an effect makes (a test holds the list to what
   the probe's effects make). Both are empty with no module, and neither changes a save or another
   counter. The report (`module-report.ts`) sets the two sweeps side by side (endings, refusals,
   fingerprints, `advance`), states each module event with its count a game and a night, the core
   events the modules' effects made, and **the delta on every core counter that moved**: every number
   of `SweepTotals` but the modules' own, by its path, a list's entries summed at the list's path and
   `[]`, with the two values, the delta and the change. It lists every counter that moved rather
   than only those the effects touch directly, since the games differ from the first effect on (no
   core stream moves because the probe drew, box 2; they move because the world differs).
7. **The run.** `HEROESIM_MODULES=probe HEROESIM_VALIDATE=1 npm run harness`, 2026-09-27, 50 seeds
   (`seed-0001` to `seed-0050`) × up to 20 years, **validated after every advance**, 16 processes,
   23.3 minutes for both sweeps; the report is `harness/reports/m8-probe-2026-09-27.md`. Both sweeps
   pass every assertion: no refused action, no validator refusal, no broken harness assertion, 50 of 50
   saves round trip, `seed-0001` replayed byte-identical. With the probe, `probe.fired` came 7,242
   times over 360,000 nights played (0.0201 a night, against a threshold of 0.02; 144.84 a game), and
   every firing applied all five effects: 7,242 each of `hero.morale-changed`,
   `guild.wealth-changed`, `hero.injured` and `quest.offered` naming the probe, and 1,137
   `patron.regard-changed` where the Regard crossed a band. 314 of the 404 core counters moved, 90 did
   not; among them `heroesInjured` +1,400 for the player's Guild and +6,302 for the Rivals (the probe's
   own 7,242 Injuries and what followed), `heroesDied` −78 and +81, Quests taken +0.9% and +0.8%, and
   the one bankruptcy with no module gone (all 50 ran 20 years with the probe). `advance` cost a mean
   2.997 ms a Turn with the probe against 2.817 ms without. Fingerprints: with the probe
   `e8fa34602a2f540596432d8f8d1fef72c189b9b11d23b66598ce0615044541bf`; with no module, over these 50
   seeds, `11a184571482f3f3f1ebe057970d72aa7ccac86b45b8930c3d12e9f5321a9e02`, the value a later
   50-seed module run's no-module sweep prints unless something moved a game.
8. **No module installed still changes nothing.** The engine's rules are untouched: the probe is a
   new file reached only through `deps.modules`, and its exports are pure. The harness's no-module
   jobs are the same JSON, and M8's counters are empty for them. The 200 × 20 proof is the M8
   close's (DL-81).

**Consequences.** The contract is proved end to end by the probe: registration, a slice made,
migrated and validated by its module, a stream no core stream notices, all three hooks, each effect
through the effects API, a stop, and the harness counting what a module did. M8-S4 installs the
probe from the front ends' test switches (`--modules probe`, a web query parameter) and words
`probe.fired`; Random Events, the first real module, adds its effect kinds to `effectEventTypes` as
it adds them to the union.

## DL-79 — Front ends and close-out: `--modules` on `new`, `load` and `advance`, a `?modules=` query parameter as the web reducer's deps, one generic sentence for any module's event, the probe in the bundle, and the first build's time counted (M8-S4)

**Status:** Accepted · **Date:** 2026-09-27 · **Decided by:** an agent (M8-S4's implementer), where
the epic names the two test switches, the generic sentence and the close-out lines but leaves their
shape open; no default, content value, `configVersion` or schema version changes, and no change to
the engine

**Context.** M8-S4 asks that the CLI and the web take a module list, empty by default: `--modules
probe` for the CLI, a query parameter for the web, both test-only (the probe is never installed by
default, nor by a front end on its own, DL-78); that both narration maps give a module event type they do
not know a generic sentence rather than a crash; that `probe.fired` be visible in both front ends'
logs on a seed known to fire one; that ADR-0005's amendment get a closing line with the tag; that
`plan.md` say the first build is complete and when, with Random Events next; and that the epics'
README get the sessions actually spent. DL-77 left M8-S4 the wording of a module's event, and DL-78
item 1 said the web build held none of the probe.

**Decision.**

1. **The CLI's switch: `--modules <ids>` on `new`, `load` and `advance`** (both of its forms),
   module ids joined by commas, each once, in the order their hooks run, from the CLI's own
   registry (`cli/src/modules.ts`, `cliModules`: only `probe`). An unknown id, an empty one or one
   named twice is a bad command line (exit 2), as the harness refuses a mistyped `HEROESIM_MODULES`
   rather than play without the module. Absent, the command is parsed as before (no `modules`
   field) and its deps carry no `modules` key, so every command writes what it wrote before M8.
   `new` makes the world with each module's slice and stream; `advance` plays its hooks; `load`
   has each module check and migrate its own slice. The other commands do not take it, as the story
   names three: they open a save with the probe's slice warning "No installed module owns the slice
   "probe": it is kept and never read", and an action writes the slice back as it was. `advance`
   without `--modules` on such a save plays without the probe, its slice and stream untouched. A
   module is installed for each invocation, as the harness installs one for each run: a save holds
   slices, not a list of the modules it was played with; the usage text says so, and data-model
   §3.4 now does too.
2. **The web's switch: the query parameter `modules`**, `?modules=probe`, comma-separated, parsed by
   `modulesFromQuery` in `web/src/state/modules.ts` (only `state/` imports engine values, M7-S2)
   and read once, as the page mounts (`App`, `useState`), so the page's modules are the same for its
   lifetime. An id the page does not know installs nothing: a page cannot refuse its own address,
   so it says what it did install instead, in its footer, "Installed for testing: the probe
   module.", and says nothing without the switch. **The modules are the reducer's deps, not its
   state:** `gameReducer(state, action, modules)` and `useGame(initial, modules)` take them, none
   by default (`noModules`), and every engine call a play makes installs them: `createWorld` for a
   new game, `deserialise` for a load, `advance`, `fastForward`, `applyAction` and `rebase`
   (`playDeps(document, modules)`, `engineDeps(modules)`). With none, the deps have no `modules`
   key, exactly the deps the reducer's tests already assert, so the page plays as it did. Modules
   are code, fixed for the page, so they are not kept in `GameState`, which the page's tests build
   and compare. A game started with the probe keeps its slice in a save kept in IndexedDB or
   exported; loaded without the parameter, the engine's `unknown-module` warning is among the load's
   warnings the page already shows.
3. **The probe is now in the web bundle.** This supersedes DL-78 item 1's "the web build holds none
   of it": a switch that works in the built page needs the probe's code there, and the Playwright
   specs, like the deployed page, run the built bundle, not the dev server. A separate test build
   would prove a bundle other than the one deployed. `npm run build -w web` passes the gate at
   495.86 kB (144.60 kB gzipped), against M7's close at 481.59 kB (140.03 kB); the difference holds
   M8-S1 to M8-S3's contract code as well as the probe, and was not separated. Once M8 is deployed,
   the public page accepts `?modules=probe`: no control on the page sets it, the footer says when it
   is on, and nothing else changes for a player who does not type it.
4. **One sentence for any module's event, in both front ends:** `The <module> module recorded
   <type> for <who>.`, the module named by the type's namespace (every module event is `<module
   id>.<what-happened>`, DL-77), then its type, then the entities it concerns by their labels,
   joined as the maps join a list: the CLI adds a Hero's id, as its other lines do ("The probe module
   recorded probe.fired for Una Greave (hero-000023), Ranulf Tarrant and The Hollin Guild."); the web
   names alone, an entity without a label by what it is ("a Hero", "someone"). With no participant
   the sentence ends at the type; a type with no namespace, which no module's `emit` makes, reads "A
   module recorded …". The payload is never read, so a payload of any shape narrates and nothing
   throws. It replaces DL-77's "A module's event: probe.fired.". Neither front end words the probe's
   own event: the probe is test-only, and a front end that words one module's events is the
   module's own UI the epic defers (§0).
5. **Box 1's seed is `modules`.** The probe draws one number a night from its own stream, seeded by
   the seed and its name alone (DL-76, DL-78), so the first night its draw falls below the threshold
   depends on the seed alone; it fires then if a Hero on a Roster stands ready, as many do in the
   first Days of a new game. On `modules` its eleventh draw is the first below 0.02: it fires on
   Turn 11, the night of Day 3, before its first stop (Day 30). Found by playing candidate seeds with the probe installed. Proved in the CLI by
   `cli/src/main.test.ts` (`new --modules probe`, `advance --turns 11 --modules probe`: the
   sentence at Turn 11, the save equal to the engine's own eleven Turns with the probe, its effects'
   events on the lines after it); in the web by `web/src/app.test.tsx` (the page opened at
   `?modules=probe` in jsdom, a game started from the form and eleven Turns advanced: the sentence at
   "Day 3, night" in "Since your last action", and without the parameter neither it nor the footer's
   line) and by `web/e2e/modules.spec.ts`, the same in the built page at both widths.
6. **The close-out lines are written as done.** ADR-0005's amendment gains a line "Closed
   2026-09-27" naming the tag `m8-modules`; `plan.md` §2's M8 row reads "Done 2026-09-27
   (`m8-modules`)" and a line under the table says the first build was completed on 2026-09-27, with
   Random Events, §4's first line, the next work. The tag and Random Events' GitHub issue are the
   orchestrator's, made right after the M8 close's tagged run (DL-81), so the epic's second box,
   "The M8 tag exists", is left unticked with a note, and M8's Status line is not set to done.
7. **The time the first build took, in the epics' README**, since it was not made in the sessions the
   estimate counts: per milestone, the wall-clock span from the first to the last commit whose
   subject begins with its name (`M3-S2: …`, `M3 verify: …`, `M3 close: …`), by committer date at
   UTC+10 from `git log --all`, merges not counted, beside the planned sessions and their 2–3 hours
   each. M8 is measured to M8-S3, the last commit before the table was written. The spans overlap,
   because agents worked several stories and milestones at once, and they hold waiting (harness
   sweeps, overnight balance passes) as well as work, so the README gives three totals and says
   which is which: the spans' sum, 90 h 26 min; the time at least one milestone was open, 42 h 39
   min; and the elapsed clock from M0's first commit (2026-09-26 00:41) to M8-S3 (2026-09-27 21:45),
   45 h 05 min, beside the 60–78 sessions (120–234 hours) planned. No record of agents' working time
   or compute was kept, and none is claimed.
8. **No module installed still changes nothing.** This story changes the CLI, the web and documents,
   not the engine; without a switch neither front end passes a `modules` key, and every existing
   CLI, reducer and page test passes unchanged but for the module sentence. The 200 × 20 byte
   identity proof is the M8 close's (DL-81).

**Consequences.** The module contract reaches both front ends: a module's events are in both logs,
its stop is said in both (DL-77), and a game made with it saves, loads and plays on with it
installed. Random Events, the first real module, will need what the probe did not: to be installed
by default, and a save that says which modules it needs, so a front end need not be told each time;
